title: The Resilience Fund pays for defense but never for the outcome: fines and awarded damages are excluded
content:
A.2.9.1.1.1.4.3.3 states the fund "[m]ust not be used to reimburse the payment of government or regulatory fines or damages awarded by the court," and A.2.9.1.1.1.4.3.2 confines claims to "losses and disbursements directly arising from a Claim Event, and reasonable legal expenses," with reasonableness defined against "average market rates of the respective jurisdiction."

The line drawn is between process cost and liability. Sky will finance the right to a competent defense; it will not absorb the consequence of losing. The rationale is incentive integrity — indemnifying fines would let a participant externalize the penalty for conduct the penalty exists to deter, and would make Sky the residual payer for every enforcement action against every contributor.

The cost is that the protection stops precisely where personal ruin begins. A contributor facing a regulatory penalty gets their lawyers paid and the fine left on them, which limits how much confidence the fund can actually buy for high-exposure roles.

Benchmarking fees to jurisdictional market rates is a quiet but real constraint: it caps the fund's exposure to premium counsel while, in practice, capping the defense a beneficiary can mount in expensive jurisdictions — the ones where enforcement risk is concentrated. The aggregate per-event cap (A.2.9.1.1.1.4.3.1) is left to risk models the Technical Committee has yet to produce.
description: Reimbursement is limited to losses and disbursements directly arising from the Claim Event plus reasonable legal expenses benchmarked to jurisdictional market rates;
